Subject: Quick ask: full subprocessor roster + EU residency notes

Hi Evelyn,

Hope you're well. As part of an internal audit for our EU deployment (CenturyTech), our security and procurement teams need two things before next Wednesday: a complete current roster of Redwood subprocessors that touch customer content for inference/observability, and a clear flag on which processors may transfer or access EU customer data outside the EU.

Specifically we need:
- CSV or table listing each subprocessor, vendor role, country(ies) of processing, and whether KMS/HSM is used.
- Any recent changes since March 2026 (additions/removals) with dates and a short reason for the change.
- If you have a short note on mitigation (VPNs, region routing, contractual clauses) for each non-EU access, that would help.

Can you share this and confirm if any of the listed subprocessors require a long lead time for removal or require additional approvals?

We have a tentative renewal conversation on 2026-06-02, so this will feed into our procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Felix

Hi Felix — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the current roster (CSV) and an annotated dataflow PDF; both include flags for EU residency and notes on KMS usage.

Quick summary:
- Current roster includes 18 subprocessors; 4 have recent changes since Mar 2026 (two added for observability, one replaced for edge caching, one decommissioned).
- Of the active subprocessors, 3 perform occasional cross-border support from US-based teams (support/maintenance only) — those rows include mitigation notes (restricted access, no content exports, VPN-only, audited jump hosts).
- All cryptographic keys for tenant data in EU regions are customer-isolated where requested; we use KMS for envelope keys on redwood side and provide HSM-backed options for Dedicated/Private customers.

Two asks from our side as follow-ups:
1) Which specific EU tenants/regions are in-scope on your side (if you can share an internal list or hubspot record, we can mark impact by tenant).
2) If CenturyTech requires vendor removal windows (e.g., must notify X days before decommission), tell us your timeline constraints so we can confirm feasibility.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-20260520.csv, eu-dataflow-annotated.pdf

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Thanks for the ping — reviewed the CSV and the change log. Quick notes: 
- Two additions (EdgeCachePro and LogStreamX) were added under standard DPA subprocessor notice in April; neither requires a DPA amendment for existing customers but we need to record them in the customer-facing roster and note the mitigation language.
- The replacement (observability vendor swap) included a data access carve-out that we already negotiated; no further approval required.
- The decommissioned vendor is already removed from Hosted routes; we should confirm export logs for the tenant range requested.

Operational removal timelines: Hosted: 7-14 days (config + cache TTL); Dedicated: depends on capacity mapping — estimate 2-4 weeks; Private/on-prem: requires a plan and Q/A window (typically 4-8 weeks).

I approve sending the annotated roster back to CenturyTech with a short cover note and the mitigation bullets. Please include a pointer to the signed DPA v3 if they ask — I attached the signed template link below.
